solves: Shows a keyboard shortcut key beside what it triggers, as a static piece.
use_when: Showing the keyboard shortcut beside the action it triggers.
Showing the shortcut in an option of nph-rich-option.
do_not_use_when: The piece would need to be clickable or receive focus — use nph-button.
The combination would come in a single piece, such as Ctrl+K — use one piece per key, side by side.

text.constraint: The text of one key, already localized by the consuming application. Empty or whitespace-only shows nothing and is not an error.

default.changes_for_user: The key appears in a box; it does not change with interaction.

business_rules: One piece per key: the combination puts the pieces side by side.
ai_hints: Use nph-kbd to show a shortcut beside what it triggers; for the action itself, use nph-button.
In a combination, put one nph-kbd per key, side by side.
Write the key through the text property; do not paint the box or the text.

accessibility.semantics: The text sits inside `<kbd>`; the host has no extra role.
accessibility.accessible_name: The screen reader announces the key by its text.
accessibility.focus: The piece does not receive focus: it has no interaction.
accessibility.contrast: color/muted-foreground on color/muted passes 4.5:1 in both schemes and in every brand.
accessibility.color_alternative: The key is written in the text; color carries no meaning.

invalid_combinations: The whole combination in a single piece — use one piece per key.
Style variant — there is no declared use.
anti_patterns: Using it as a button or control.
Painting the box or the text by hand.

sources.design_md: design.md, text/label-sm, color/muted, color/muted-foreground, color/border, border/width, radius/inner and space/inline-tight
sources.decision: P66 — API and semantics of nph-spinner, nph-separator and nph-kbd, 05-10-2026
sources.usage_evidence: nph-rich-option, through the option of showing a shortcut
